summary: Feed c049_nic_span is severely degraded: 56.33% packet loss due to SPAN oversubscription (2.29 Gbps mirrored into 1 Gbps destination) plus 2.88% loss at IDS eth1. IDS receives only ~43% of intended traffic, breaking detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: SPAN oversubscription at DC-CORE-1: source Gi1/0/1 mirrors 42,937,440 packets (2.29 Gbps) into destination Gi1/0/48 which is only 1 Gbps. Switch discards 24,187,500 packets on output (56.33% lost, average load 100% with higher bursts). Downstream IDS eth1 (1 Gbps per tool profile) also discards 539,460 packets (2.88% of what arrived) because capture interface cannot keep up with bursts.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS (needs both directions and full payload) misses >56% of traffic before it arrives, plus additional tool drops. Random SPAN drops break flow reassembly, miss both directions of sessions, cause signature misses and false negatives. Effective detection coverage <44%.

params.broker_requirement: connect TAP to packet broker with 10G capture, then load_balance or filter to fit 1G IDS capacity - e.g., load-balance 2.29 Gbps across 3x 1G IDS or upgrade IDS to 10G

recommended_fix.why: TAP forwards 100% losslessly unlike SPAN which drops when mirrored rate exceeds destination rate. Packet broker buffers microbursts and can distribute/filter the 2.29 Gbps aggregate so neither the switch SPAN port nor the 1G IDS interface is oversubscribed, restoring complete traffic to IDS.
